validity.recommendation: Keep the row; it is a real, correctly-classified project. Fix stale ownership/dates/cost/endpoint per the other concern objects.
validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE: strongly confirmed and highly active. The subsea gas export line from Cyprus's Aphrodite field (Block 12, ~170 km offshore Limassol, ~3.5-3.7 tcf) to Egypt is documented across many independent 2025-2026 sources. Cyprus approved the updated development plan Feb 2025 (oedigital); FEED for the production systems AND the transmission/pipeline infrastructure was sanctioned 22 Dec 2025 with a ~USD 105.7M budget (rigzone, offshore-energy); a term sheet + host-government agreement for the pipeline was signed with EGAS in April 2026 (worldoil, enterpriseam). CLASSIFICATION: correct — a gas transmission (export trunk) subsea pipeline; Fuel=Gas and PipelineType=transmission both stand. DUPLICATE: none. Distinct from the Israel–Egypt lines (P3620/P3657, Leviathan/Israeli source) and from P7597 Cronos–Port Said (ENI's Cronos field, different source field) — even though the latest Aphrodite deal also lands gas at Port Said, the source field is different, so not a duplicate.

validity.recommendation: Update owners to Chevron 35% (operator) / Shell (BG Cyprus) 35% / NewMed Energy 30%; drop Noble Energy and Delek Group.
validity.researcher_notes: OWNERSHIP is STALE/WRONG. GEM records Owner1=Shell 35%, Owner2=Noble Energy 35%, Owner3=Delek Group 30%. Current Aphrodite partners are Chevron (operator, via Chevron Cyprus Ltd) 35%, Shell (BG Cyprus Ltd) 35%, and NewMed Energy 30% — confirmed by egyptoil-gas, oedigital, offshore-energy, and NewMed Energy's own operations page. Chevron acquired Noble Energy in Oct 2020 (so Noble's 35% is now Chevron's), and Delek Group's E&P arm (Delek Drilling) was renamed NewMed Energy in 2021 (so 'Delek Group' should read 'NewMed Energy'). Note: the pipeline itself is slated to be built/operated by a new SPC, 'Aphrodite Midstream,' jointly owned by the field partners plus an Egyptian government entity (enterpriseam) — a distinct owner/operator from the upstream field once formed.

validity.recommendation: Verify/update endpoint: latest (April 2026) term sheet lands gas at a Port Said onshore metering station, not the Damietta SEGAS LNG terminal.
validity.researcher_notes: ENDPOINT likely stale. GEM has EndLocation='Damietta Segas LNG Terminal', EndState/Province='Damietta'. Earlier (2018-2022) plans did target the Damietta area, but the April 2026 EGAS/Chevron term sheet states gas will land at Port Said, with the final delivery point set at the metering station at the onshore terminal in Port Said (worldoil, enterpriseam). Start point (Aphrodite offshore field, Cyprus) and EndCountryOrArea=Egypt are correct. Recommend updating the Egyptian landing point to Port Said (or noting both, since routing to Damietta LNG via existing infrastructure has also been floated).

validity.recommendation: Fix dates and cost: blank/clear ConstructionYear=2025 (construction not started; slated 2027), change StartYear1 2028->2030 (grid)/2031 (field first gas), update SegmentCost $1bn->$2bn; treat Length=310 km as unverified.
validity.researcher_notes: Multiple SPEC fields are stale or unsupported. (1) ConstructionYear=2025 is WRONG — what happened in Dec 2025 was the FEED decision, not construction; pipeline construction is slated for 2027 (enterpriseam, oedigital FID-in-2027). (2) StartYear1=2028 is stale — first gas is now targeted at 2030 (delivery to Egypt's grid/LNG) with field supply commencing 2031 (oedigital, enterpriseam). The existing attaqa.net ref for 2028 does not even contain the value (screen failed). (3) SegmentCost=USD 1,000,000,000 is stale — that is the 2018 Reuters $800M-$1B estimate; the Feb 2026 host-government agreement puts the pipeline at ~USD 2 billion (Cyprus to fund it) (worldoil, enterpriseam). (Note separately the upstream field development plan is ~$4bn — not the pipeline.) (4) LengthKnown=310 km could NOT be independently corroborated — sources cite ~170 km field-to-Limassol distance and one report of a ~110 km subsea link tying into existing (Zohr) infrastructure; no independent source states 310 km. Leave as unverified pending a sourced figure; do not treat as confirmed. Capacity=8 bcm/y is broadly consistent with the ~800 MMcf/d max field/plateau (~8.3 bcm/y), though the contracted delivery is up to 700 MMcf/d for the first six years.

status_reviews.researcher_notes: Status 'proposed' is still correct and NOT stale — the project is highly active but pre-FID and pre-construction. FEED for production + transmission infrastructure sanctioned 22 Dec 2025 (rigzone). April 2026 term sheet + host-government agreement signed with EGAS (enterpriseam/worldoil). June 2026: Egypt's oil ministry pushing a September 2026 deadline to finalize the main agreements, with FID committed for 2027 (enterpriseam, oedigital). Construction slated 2027, first gas 2030/field supply 2031. No FID and no ground broken, so it has not advanced to 'construction'; abundant 2025-2026 progress rules out any dormancy/staleness downgrade. Most recent independent evidence: June 2026.

fills.researcher_notes: FIDStatus=Pre-FID confirmed: partners are committed to take FID in 2027 (Cyprus PSC amendment / oedigital); as of June 2026 the main agreements are targeted for finalization by September 2026, still ahead of FID (enterpriseam). Consider adding FIDYear=2027 (target).

GEM's 8.00 bcm/y is a reasonable annualization of the plateau/FPU max of ~800 MMcf/d cited by oedigital and egyptoil-gas (~8.3 bcm/y). Caveat: the contracted delivery to Egypt is up to 700 MMcf/d for the first six years before flexible volumes (~7.2 bcm/y), so 8 bcm/y reflects nameplate rather than contracted throughput. Medium tier because sources state MMcf/d, not the bcm/y figure directly.

Start (Aphrodite offshore field, Cyprus) and end country (Egypt) are confirmed. Only refs added for the confirmed endpoints — the specific Egyptian landing point (Damietta vs Port Said) is flagged as an attribution concern above; the April 2026 term sheet points to Port Said, so EndLocation/EndState should be revisited before locking a ref for those subfields.

Could NOT independently corroborate LengthKnown=310 km. Sources give ~170 km (field-to-Limassol, i.e. field location, not pipeline) and one report of a ~110 km subsea tie-in to existing (Zohr) infrastructure toward Damietta. No independent source states 310 km. Left UNRESOLVED per standing rule 2 — no fabricated ref. Recommend re-checking against the FEED/host-government route once published.

summary: P0473 Cyprus–Egypt (Aphrodite) real + correctly classified (transmission gas), status 'proposed' confirmed (FEED Dec 2025, FID 2027, first gas 2030/31); concerns: stale ownership (Noble->Chevron, Delek->NewMed), endpoint likely Port Said not Damietta, and stale specs (ConstructionYear 2025, StartYear1 2028->2030/31, cost $1bn->$2bn); Length 310 km UNRESOLVED.
